contents.name: Static spatial geometry and charged background data

source_review.limitations: The local definition adds compactness, smoothness and SI units and proves its own product-metric signature and volume-density well-definedness.

contents.name: Stationary zero-derivative pressure functional and long-wavelength qualification

source_review.read_extent: Read §§1.1–1.2, including eqs. (1.3)–(1.12), and checked the charged-sector W0 expression and its relation to omitted derivative corrections.
source_review.supports: The adopted local-pressure integral, Tolman redshifted temperature profile, charged background dependence, and the characterization of W0 as the zero-derivative contribution.
source_review.limitations: The source treats a field-theory partition trace and natural-unit/gauge conventions; the local postulate is a separately adopted effective functional and asserts no trace construction or microscopic convergence.

contents.name: Chemical-potential differentiation of the equilibrium partition function

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.3.1, eqs. (2.15)–(2.24), including the fixed-background derivative convention and charge relation Q=T0 times the mu0 derivative of W.
source_review.supports: The physical interpretation of a parameter derivative of the adopted effective functional; the local proof independently computes both derivatives and the positivity implication.
source_review.limitations: The source does not state the local C2 compact-manifold differentiation proof or its SI kB factor; those are supplied explicitly in the local conditional proof.

sources.title: Pavel Kovtun, Lectures on hydrodynamic fluctuations in relativistic theories
sources.locator: Complete 55-page lecture notes retrieved. §1.3, PDF pp. 4–14, for constitutive gradient counting and the microscopic mean-free-path scale; §2.6, PDF p. 30, for the microscopic time-scale/mean-free-time qualification; §3.2, PDF pp. 34–35, for the fluctuation-induced limitation on a second-order local derivative expansion.

contents.name: Derivative expansion and microscopic length scale

source_review.read_extent: Read §1.3, especially the paragraphs defining the derivative expansion and comparing its cutoff with the microscopic mean-free-path scale.
source_review.supports: The requirement to state a long-wavelength regime and a microscopic scale when adopting a truncated hydrostatic/effective description.
source_review.limitations: The notes identify a mean free path for their fluid model; the local item requires each application to name its own relevant microscopic scale and does not identify distinct microscopic lengths universally.

contents.name: Microscopic relaxation time limits time-dependent hydrodynamic use

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.6/PDF p. 30, including the explicit identification of a microscopic time scale and mean-free time between collisions and the requirement that hydrodynamic time scales be much longer.
source_review.supports: The postulate separately requires a declared microscopic relaxation time for any time-dependent extension of the effective description.
source_review.limitations: The source time scale is model-dependent and is not identified with every transport or stress-relaxation coefficient; the static functional itself contains no temporal gradients.
